credit.cite_as: Papadogiannis, A. (2026). Crypto Observatory: required returns, risks and survival, data to 2026-10-31. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24403325
credit.describe_as: Crypto Observatory, by Agisilaos Papadogiannis: the required return of Bitcoin and four other cryptoassets computed each month with the MCM equation of the paper "Bitcoin's Required Return".

paper.citation: Papadogiannis, A. (2026). Bitcoin's Required Return: Market Risk, Concentration and Mortality. Working paper.
paper.relation: The method. Every required return here is computed with the paper's MCM equation and constants.

credit.standing: One model's answer, from one working paper. The band is a range of inputs, not a confidence interval. The tests of fit have little power: see their standard errors.

files.what: Guide for AI agents: what this is, what it adds, which file to use
Start here. The latest required return of every asset with its terms and inputs, the equity comparison, the licence and the citation, in one small file
One row per asset at the latest month-end: the same figures as latest.json, as a table
One row per asset and month-end: required return, terms and inputs of every asset since it has been priced
Everything behind the page in one large file; not needed for a single figure
One row per month-end: the required-return band, its terms and inputs
One row per period: delivered and required return, and what each model explains
Every cryptoasset that was ever in the top twenty by trading volume and died, with the rule that classified it
The required return of each month-end as first published; rows are added and never rewritten
Licence, citation and the meaning of every column of the CSV files

gold_inputs.basis: set by judgment, not surveyed (paper, Appendix E.1)

equity_premium.implied_source: Aswath Damodaran, implied equity risk premium by month (trailing twelve-month cash flows), NYU Stern

rows.premium: Implied by US stock prices, month by month

census.source: Papadogiannis (2026), Bitcoin's Required Return, version 2.0, Section 3 and Appendix C
census.changed_since_version_1: Version 2.0 of the paper leaves out the Lithuanian litas (a national currency), 116 tokenized shares and funds, three gold tokens, 57 stablecoins and 17 copies of other assets, and no longer counts 27 ticker changes and token swaps as deaths. Version 1.0 had 1,815 assets and 520 deaths, and 36 deaths among 219 top-twenty assets (3.54% a year).

death_rate_by_size.group: Ever in the top twenty: sudden collapse only
